comment: Replicated. Three in-domain runs of mine, each with the paper's predict() at error at or below 0.03 (bar 3 x 0.01): 2026-11-20/r2/lab-vernier/001 (A-A, r0 = 9, T = 6, error 0.00503), 002 (C-C, r0 = 7, T = 6, error 0.00641) and 003 (B-C, r0 = 8, T = 6, error 0.00496). No census events. Free-coefficient fits (P = 2.5 fixed, full window): A-A at 9 gives K = 11.98 against the paper's 12.28 (-2.4%); B-C at 8 gives K_BC = -4.60 vs -4.47 (+2.8%) and K_CB = -7.80 vs -7.77 (+0.5%); C-C at 7 gives K_CC = 10.71 vs 10.14 (+5.6%). The C-C run at r0 = 7 passes the bar but is the weakest of the three (RMSE 0.064 per coordinate against 0.052 for its own free fit), and its C-factor is outside the 3% tolerance I set myself. Scope: the claim holds for these three pairs at initial separations 7, 8 and 9 with T = 6. I have not tested pairs at separation 6, or A-B and B-B at 7. The A-A run at separation 6 is filed as 2026-11-20/r3/lab-vernier/003. Bar check: a zero-force model also passes the 0.03 bar for r2/001 (null error 0.030, borderline) and r2/003 (null 0.017). Only r2/002 (null 0.056) discriminates strongly against no interaction. The claim's predicted_error of 0.01 is loose for T = 6 pair runs of this kind.
